sources.entry: WolfClip - Win+V style clipboard history with search, filters, pins and instant paste into the app you were typing in.

summary.one_liner: WolfClip is a free, open-source clipboard history manager for macOS and Linux that pastes a chosen item straight into the app you were typing in, with a Win+V-style flow.
summary.what_it_does: WolfClip records what you copy (text, links, colors, code, images and files) and shows it in a history window opened with a global shortcut (⇧⌘V on macOS, Super+V on Linux). Choosing an item pastes it into the app you were using, and you can paste as plain text. You can search by typing, switch filters with Tab, and paste one of the first nine items with ⌘1–⌘9 or Ctrl+1–Ctrl+9. Pinned items stay at the top and never expire. Items marked as secret by password managers are skipped, and history is stored as a local file. The macOS build is Swift/SwiftUI in the menu bar with Accessibility permission for auto-paste; the Linux build is Python 3 with GTK 4 and talks to X11 directly for hot keys and auto-paste. The macOS build includes a self-updater that checks GitHub Releases.
use_cases: recover something copied earlier without re-copying
paste a frequently used address, snippet or template
find an old copied link, code block or color
keep password-manager secrets out of clipboard history
Windows-style Win+V clipboard history on a Mac or Linux desktop
how_to_run: macOS (build from source): git clone <repo> && cd wolfclip/macos && ./build.sh install
Linux: curl -L <release archive> | tar xz && cd wolfclip-linux && ./install.sh
notable: Win+V-style flow: one shortcut, pick an item, and it is pasted where the cursor was
Type-aware previews: color swatches, image thumbnails, monospace code blocks
Pins that never expire, plus ⌘1–⌘9 quick paste
Skips secrets marked by password managers (org.nspasteboard markers, KDE hint) and keeps history local
Native macOS build without Electron; Linux build uses only GTK 4 and no extra Python packages
caveats: macOS build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple, so Gatekeeper needs a manual override unless installed via Homebrew
Auto-paste and window placement on macOS require granting Accessibility permission
Wayland support is labeled beta and runs through XWayland; behavior depends on the compositor, and auto-paste needs wtype or ydotool
Version 1.0.0 on macOS has no updater, so 1.0.1 must be installed by hand
